nodes.label: Numerical Representation
nodes.description: All new media objects are composed of digital code.

nodes.label: Modularity
nodes.description: The fractal structure of new media where elements are assembled but maintain their independent structure.

nodes.label: Automation
nodes.description: Numerical coding and modular structure allow for the automation of many operations involved in media creation, manipulation, and access.

nodes.label: Variability
nodes.description: A new media object is not something fixed once and for all, but something that can exist in different, potentially infinite versions.

nodes.label: Transcoding
nodes.description: The translation of media into another format, typically reflecting the influence of the computer's logic on cultural logic.

nodes.label: Cultural Interfaces
nodes.description: Interfaces to cultural data shaped by the printed word, cinema, and human-computer interaction (HCI).

nodes.label: Compositing
nodes.description: The process of combining various digital media elements into a single, seamless moving image or virtual space.

nodes.label: Teleaction
nodes.description: Acting at a distance in real time, shifting from representation to communication.

nodes.label: Synthetic Realism
nodes.description: The visual style and illusionism specific to computer-generated 3D graphics.

nodes.label: Database Logic
nodes.description: Structuring cultural objects as collections of individual items rather than sequential narratives.

nodes.label: Navigable Space
nodes.description: Organizing data or virtual worlds as architectural spaces that the user can explore.

nodes.label: Digital Cinema
nodes.description: Moving images constructed or heavily manipulated through digital software, merging live-action with animation and painting.

nodes.label: Spatial Montage
nodes.description: Presenting different images or media elements simultaneously on a single screen rather than sequentially in time.
